symptom.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by at least one full manic episode, often with marked functional impairment, that may be accompanied by delusions or hallucinations congruent or incongruent with mood. Episodes typically develop over days to weeks and can last weeks to months, with intervening periods of partial or full remission; depressive episodes are common but not required for diagnosis. Psychotic features usually emerge at the more severe end of mania or depression and help distinguish Bipolar I from Bipolar II and cyclothymia, as well as from primary psychotic disorders like schizophrenia where mood symptoms are not as prominent or temporally linked. The course is often recurrent, influenced by stress, sleep disruption, and biological vulnerability, and may be complicated by impaired insight, risky behavior, and strained social and occupational functioning.

patient.stressor: For Sara, the onset coincided with a period of rapid growth at her startup, where she was promoted and tasked with overseeing multiple new product launches while informally mentoring junior staff and studying for the GMAT in her spare time. What began as long hours and high energy at work escalated over a few weeks into an unsustainable pace: back‑to‑back meetings, late‑night strategy sessions at coffee shops, and weekend travel for networking events, with her normal exercise and social routines becoming increasingly erratic. Over the following two months, colleagues noticed her becoming increasingly forceful and difficult to interrupt in meetings, dominating discussions and sending streams of late‑night messages about sweeping process overhauls that were only loosely connected to the team’s plans. The situation reached a crisis when a senior executive confronted her about her behavior after she spoke nonstop through a presentation and derailed a major client call, and HR strongly recommended she seek an urgent psychiatric evaluation before returning to full responsibilities.
patient.chief_complaint: “Once I start talking, I just can’t seem to stop—I feel like I have to get every idea out all at once and people keep telling me I’m overwhelming them.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Lately I've been completely convinced that the CEO and the board are secretly tracking my emails and Slack messages because they realized I’ve cracked some big strategy that could change the whole industry, and no matter how many times HR tells me that’s not happening, it still feels obvious to me that every meeting and comment is really about testing whether I’m loyal enough to share it with them.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I’m alone at night working on my laptop, I keep hearing this clear male voice just over my shoulder telling me things like, “Push harder, you’re the chosen one for this,” or sometimes, if I slow down, “You’re wasting time, they’re watching,” even though I know there’s nobody actually there and it’s not coming from my headphones or anything.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Most days I’m either buzzing and on top of the world, like I’m running the whole company and nothing can touch me, or I flip on a dime and snap at people over tiny things—like someone questioning one of my ideas—because it suddenly feels like they’re trying to sabotage me or hold me back.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I wake up after just a couple of hours of sleep feeling wired, and then I’ll pace around my apartment, reorganize my closet, start drafting new product plans, and still feel like I physically cannot sit still or slow down enough to just watch a show or read a book like I used to.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: In meetings and even in this kind of conversation, it’s like my mouth can’t keep up with my brain and I feel this constant pressure to keep talking and explaining every connection I see, so I barrel over people, jump from idea to idea, and only realize everyone’s exhausted or annoyed when they tell me afterward that they couldn’t get a word in.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My thoughts are running so fast that by the time I finish one sentence in my head I’ve already started three more, jumping from a marketing idea to a GMAT math shortcut to some grand plan to spin off a new division, and I can’t find an off switch even when I’m lying in bed at 3 a.m. begging my brain to just shut up for a while.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: I’ve been taking on new projects at work, sketching out side-business ideas, signing up for extra GMAT practice sessions, booking networking trips on a whim, and pinging people constantly on LinkedIn and text, to the point where I’m juggling so many “big moves” at once that nothing ever really gets finished but I still feel compelled to start the next thing.
